author: reek
body: What an agent knows about the ORDER of a library -- its own after a scry, brainstorm, or tutor-to-top, or an opponent's after a mill or reveal. Library manipulation grants positional knowledge: a card placed on top is the next draw, a card placed Nth from the top is known at that depth, a card sent to the bottom is known to be there. That knowledge is fragile -- the instant the library is shuffled, or cards go back in a random order, the ordering is gone and the model must forget it. Modelling this correctly is what separates an agent that "plays to its outs" from one that guesses.

author: reek
body: top-known is an ordered window from the top: index 0 is the top card (the next draw), index 1 the second, and so on. A slot holding no-card means the agent knows a card sits there but not which -- the residue of a random reordering.

author: reek
body: A shuffle randomises the whole library: every positional fact is now false, so the agent forgets all of it, top and bottom alike.

author: reek
body: Putting k cards back on top in a random order: the agent knows a card occupies each of the top k slots but not which, and the previously known cards are now k deeper. Ordering knowledge of those slots is destroyed -- they become no-card.

author: reek
body: Wiring glue: consume a draw only when the library actually shrank (the draw step is skipped on the first turn). The engine passes the library size before and after the draw step; a smaller after means one card left the top.
